question: How accurately can we recover a regression mean or treatment effect simultaneously along an entire boundary when each query uses outcomes and distances rather than full locations? Ordinary signed-distance local polynomial fits provide pointwise results and probability control, which do not establish either accuracy everywhere on the boundary or expected loss on unusual samples.
result: Write a_n=(log n/n)^(1/4). For unsigned observations, the minimax expected supremum error R_n^PI over P_NP(L,q) satisfies liminf R_n^PI/a_n ≥ c_PI>0 for integer q≥1 and L≥4, even when a different law-independent rule is selected at each query. This class imposes compact two-dimensional support, a Lipschitz boundary, bounded positive density and variance, and bounded regression derivatives through order q−1 with Lipschitz highest derivative. For signed observations, R_n^{12,±} is the minimax expected supremum error for τ_P(x)=E[Y(1)|X=x]−E[Y(0)|X=x] over the treatment boundary. For integer p≥0, ν≥2, and L≥L_0(p)≥48, liminf R_n^{12,±}/a_n ≥ c>0, already with fixed rectangular geometry. The signed class requires bounded positive density, smooth arm means, bounded conditional 2+ν moments, and local slice mass, neighborhood mass, and stable population designs on both arms. Under distance identification, uniform O(h) population intercept bias, and the joint expected sampling bounds of slide 9, limsup R_n^{12,±}/a_n ≤ C. Specifically, the stabilized local polynomial estimator with h_n=a_n and B_n=a_n^(−1/3) satisfies sup_P E_P^*[sup_{x∈B_P}|τ̂_{n,h_n}(x)−τ_P(x)|] ≤ Ca_n eventually. Its upper bound applies for L≥4; matching the lower bound requires L≥L_0(p).
mechanism: 1. Place many separated smooth bumps along a boundary, each controlled by a binary choice and changing the target at its center by Δ. Smoothness allows width w proportional to Δ^(1/q) and approximately Δ^(−1/q) choices. 2. Pair each enabled bump with an angular density tilt. Left–right reflection preserves radius and treatment side, so the tilt preserves distance probabilities. Its interaction with the horizontal baseline cancels the bump in the pooled outcome law outside a central radius of order Δ. Binary outcomes, or the unsigned construction’s mixture law linear in its mean, make cancellation of the pooled mean sufficient to cancel the whole observed outcome law. 3. The remaining region has area of order Δ² and outcome-probability separation of order Δ. Thus conditional one-observation divergence is O(Δ⁴/w²). Multiplying by the expected observations in a disk gives block divergence O(nΔ⁴). 4. Poissonize the sample to obtain independent cell blocks. Give each decoder its own compressed block and every other block with raw locations; this view can reproduce an admissible query rule. 5. Couple the two alternatives within each cell so their compressed blocks sometimes agree. On any realized array containing an overlap, flipping an overlapping coordinate leaves that coordinate’s decoder input unchanged. Pairing choice vectors therefore forces a decoding error somewhere for at least half the vectors. Independence of the coupled cell pairs and a standard divergence-to-overlap bound make such overlaps sufficiently likely. 6. Choose nΔ⁴ proportional to log M, with a sufficiently small constant. This yields Δ proportional to a_n. Uniform estimation error below Δ/2 would decode every choice, so decoding failure gives the expected supremum-error lower bound. An exponentially unlikely Poisson sample shortage permits transfer back to n observations. 7. For attainment, winsorize outcomes, fit separate distance polynomials, guard matrix inversion, subtract intercepts, and clip the result. Balance population bias, truncation error, expected residual fluctuations, and the loss from unstable designs using h=a_n and B=h^(−1/3).
why_true: Distance discards the angular information that would reveal the compensating density change. Only a small central region distinguishes each alternative, producing fourth-power information. Many possible hidden changes impose the logarithmic cost of simultaneous recovery; coupling handles their shared observations without assuming independent decoder successes. For attainment, identification connects distance intercepts to the target, the bias assumption controls approximation, and winsorization supplies bounded contributions with controlled tail error. The inversion guard limits amplification. Expected Gram control bounds the probability of an unstable design, while clipping bounds its loss, so unusual samples are included in expected-risk control.
example: The fixed square support with treatment rectangle [−1,1]×[0,2] provides a worked construction. At bottom-edge centers, τ_Pω(x_j)=x_j^(1)/16+ω_jΔ. Within a treated semicircle, the baseline varies by rη/16. Multiplying by the density tilt −32Δφ/r contributes −2Δφη²; averaging η² over the semicircle gives 1/2 and cancels the added Δφ. Signed distance still reveals treatment side, but it hides the left–right direction needed to detect this compensation.

findings.problem: The displayed BiasRatio expression uses an unexplained function name whose mathematical content is supplied in the following paragraph. I understand the assumption, but cannot read its object directly from the formula.
findings.fix: Display the ratio explicitly as sup_P sup_{x∈B_P}|e_1ᵀ(β*_{1,P,x}(h_n)−β*_{0,P,x}(h_n))−τ_P(x)|/h_n, defining β* as the population local polynomial coefficients.

findings.problem: ScoreDev is described as error in polynomial-weighted raw-outcome averages, without displaying the average or its population counterpart. Its relationship to the winsorized residual score introduced later is harder to retain.
findings.fix: Show ScoreDev as the supremum of the empirical raw-outcome moment vector minus its population expectation, and add that it differs from the winsorized residual score; the attainment argument uses the package’s Gram bound.

findings.problem: The residual score and the coefficient-error identity are only described in words, immediately before a substantial maximal-bound formula. These are the connecting objects that explain how the bound controls the estimator.
findings.fix: Display score^B=m̂^B−Ψ̂β* and β̂^B−β*=Ψ̂^(−1)score^B on the guarded branch. Use those identities to connect the existing fluctuation bound to coefficient error.
